title: Pipit and the Lost Book
markdown:
The cozy reading nook was quieter than usual. Pipit the puppy and Marmalade the teddy were the very best of friends. Pipit was a fluffy little puppy, with ears that wiggled like happy worms and a tail that wagged with so much joy. Marmalade was his soft ginger-colored bear, button eyes and a smile stitched with kindness. Pipit’s favorite thing was to snuggle with Marmalade.

Tonight the playroom felt a little bit different. Pipit sniffed the air.

“Marmalade,” he whispered. “It’s story time. Where is our book?”

Pipit loved their bedtime stories. But tonight their special book, the one with the bright blue cover, was gone. A tiny flutter, like a trapped butterfly, began in Pipit’s tummy. When things were not where they ought to be, his happy tail would droop just a little. His floppy ears would press back, and he would feel wobbly, like a leaf in a gentle breeze. He did not name the feeling. He only looked at the empty nook where the blue cover should have been.

“Now, Pipit, don’t you worry,” Marmalade said. His voice was soft, like warm moss. “We will find it together. Let’s look outside our nook.”

Pipit took a little breath. If the book wasn’t found before the last sunbeam faded, he would miss story time. And that would be very sad indeed. With a brave little thump of his tail, Pipit stepped out from the blankets. The playroom felt bigger now. The toy chest seemed taller. The curtains whispered. But Marmalade was right beside him, his paw on Pipit’s back.

They padded softly to the big toy chest. Pipit lowered his nose and sniffed. His whiskers twitched.

“Not here, Marmalade.”

Marmalade nodded. Next they tiptoed to the velvet curtains. Pipit and Marmalade peeked behind them. The sunlight made dancing patterns on the floor. But there was no blue book. Pipit felt that flutter in his tummy again. He sat down for a moment, his tail giving a small swish. He almost wished he could go back to their nook and forget the worry. He felt a little scared of the unknown rustling behind the curtains.

“Pipit, look!” Marmalade pointed a fuzzy paw. He had found a big soft mound of cushions, piled up like colorful little hills. And peeking out from the very top of one cushion was a sliver of bright blue.

“The book!” Pipit yipped. His tail began to thump, thump, thump. He wiggled with happiness.

Pipit nudged the soft cushions with his nose. He pushed them aside, one by one. It felt like a small mountain to climb. He paused. It was a lot of cushions. But then he thought of the wonderful stories and Marmalade’s gentle nudge. He took a deep breath and kept going. With one last push, the book was free.

Pipit carefully picked it up. Then, with Marmalade by his side, they trotted back to their cozy reading nook. It felt even cozier now. Pipit gently put the book on Marmalade’s lap. His tail gave a happy wag.

Now Pipit snuggled down. Marmalade settled beside him. The book lay open between them. The flutter in Pipit’s tummy was all gone. He felt warm and happy. He had found the book, even when he felt wobbly. Later that evening a little ladybug landed on Pipit’s nose. It tickled. Instead of wiggling away, Pipit just gave a soft sniff and a little wag. The soft glow of the room was like a warm blanket. His tail gave a contented thump. He did not ask whoooo knew that finding a lost book could feel so wonderful, or decide that with a good friend he could always find his way. He only opened the blue cover to the first page, Marmalade’s stitched smile catching the last sunbeam, and let story time begin where it had always belonged.
